newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to meet Israeli defence chief.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to meet Israeli defence chief.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat planned to urge Israel's defence chief on Wednesday to carry out a troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron and stop expanding Jewish settlements, PLO officials said.

"We will ask (Yitzhak) Mordechai to implement interim agreements, especially redeployment from Hebron, to lift the closure (on the West Bank and Gaza) and revoke orders to... build more settlements and demolish Arab homes," Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said.
Hours before Mordechai was to meet Arafat for the first time, news emerged he had approved the building of an additional 1,800 housing units in a Jewish settlement in the West Bank.

Israel's Peace Now group said the planned privately-funded construction in the ultraorthodox settlement of Matityahu was the largest housing project approved by the government for Jews in the West Bank since it came to power in June.
"We are speaking of plans which were approved in the past by the previous (Labour-led) government and frozen, and now they have been reapproved," a Defence Ministry spokeswoman said.
PLO officials said Arafat also would meet U.S. peace coordinator Dennis Ross on Wednesday after the envoy's arrival from Egypt, where he held talks with President Hosni Mubarak.

The Arafat-Mordechai meeting was scheduled for last week following the Palestinian president's September 4 summit with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but was delayed due to what officials described as busy schedules.

Mordechai is the architect of a new redeployment plan for Hebron that is likely to leave more Israeli troops in the city than was envisaged in the original agreement signed by the previous government.
Israel's new right-wing administration has said changes are necessary to ensure security for the 400 Jews who have settled among more than 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron.

"If Mordechai sumbits requests for changing the agreement, we will refuse because we reject renegotiating or modifying any signed agreement," said Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, general secretary of the Palestinian Presidency.

The long-delayed redeployment was scheduled for last March, but the previous government postponed the partial troop pullout after Moslem suicide bombers killed 59 people in Israel in a series of attacks.
Hebron is the last of seven West Bank cities to be handed over to Palestinians under an interim PLO-Israel peace deal.
Palestinians view redeployment from Hebron as a test of Israeli intentions to pursue the peace process.
Israel has also missed a September 7 date for initiating further redeployments from parts of the West Bank still under occupation.
Palestinians, frustrated over a lack of progress in talks with Israel, have asked for U.S. intervention to pressure Netanyahu to implement peace accords.

U.N. special envoy Terje Larsen said Ross also would attend a meeting in Gaza to discuss with the PLO and donor representatives results of a recent meeting of international donors to assist the Palestinian economy.
On another front, Syria said on Wednesday that Netanyahu's policies had caused tension in the region and could lead to war.
The remarks, which appeared in Syria's official press, were the latest sign of tension between the two countries, fuelled by Syrian troop movements in Lebanon.

Syria in recent weeks has moved up to 12,000 troops -- around a third of its force in Lebanon -- closer to Israel's border, some to within striking range of key Israeli positions in the Golan Heights.
